rows.title: Macklem says inflation forecast is lower, but oil price pressures are lingering
rows.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said in a Toronto speech and press conference that recent drops in gasoline prices mean inflation could finish 2026 below the bank's October forecast of about 3.5%. He warned, however, that cost increases built up over the past eight months, largely from oil prices pushed up by the Middle East war, have not fully reached consumers yet. Canadian inflation held at 3.1% in October, and price pressure has spread beyond gas to groceries and clothing. The speech also presented the renewed 2027-2031 inflation-control framework, which keeps the 2% target for total CPI and refocuses on the CPIX and CPI-trim core measures. Markets raised the odds of another quarter-point hike at the December 9 decision to about 79% from roughly 63% the day before.
rows.fact: Macklem said falling gas prices could leave year-end inflation below the October forecast, but businesses have so far absorbed much of the higher production and transport costs, and the bank's surveys point to more pass-through to consumer prices. The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.5% in October, and October CPI inflation was 3.1%. Under the renewed framework, the 2% target applies to total CPI, with CPIX and CPI-trim as the main core gauges.
rows.outlook: CIBC chief economist Avery Shenfeld read Macklem's focus on lingering cost pressures as a sign the bank could raise rates again on December 9, after it weighs third-quarter GDP and November jobs data.
rows.why: 중앙은행이 유가 같은 공급 충격이 물가 전반으로 번지는 '2차 효과'를 왜 경계하며, 휘발유 값이 내려도 금리 인상을 고민하는지 보여 주기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why a central bank worries about supply shocks like oil spreading into all prices, and why it may still consider a rate hike even as gas prices fall.
rows.term_def: When a cost increase for businesses, such as higher fuel or shipping costs, gets passed on to customers as higher prices for many other goods. Central banks watch it because it can make inflation last longer.
rows.note: Today's policy item (BoC governor's speech and framework, Nov 24 ET). Framework details cross-checked with the Bank of Canada's speech page and the CP story on core measures; market odds per LSEG as cited by CP.

opinion.title: CIBC flags December rate hike as Macklem doubles down on inflation concerns
opinion.outlet: Investing.com (reporting a CIBC Capital Markets note)
opinion.author: Jaiveer Shekhawat
opinion.summary: After Macklem's speech, CIBC economists moved their call for the Bank of Canada's next rate hike forward from January to the December 9 meeting. They read the governor as more worried about energy costs spreading into wider prices than reassured by softer underlying inflation, and noted he played down three straight monthly job declines and 6.7% unemployment. CIBC argues that another hike from the low end of the bank's neutral range would mostly remove stimulus rather than squeeze the economy. It sees a possible pause in January if inflation outside energy stays low, and a long hold in 2027 once the war-driven jump in energy prices drops out of the year-over-year figures after February.
opinion.why: 같은 연설을 두고 시장 전문가가 금리 전망을 어떻게 바꾸는지, 그리고 '중립금리'와 기저효과 개념이 실제 전망에 어떻게 쓰이는지 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how market economists change their rate forecasts after a central bank speech and how ideas like the neutral rate and base effects shape those forecasts.

rows.title: US inflation rises further in October
rows.summary: The Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that the PCE price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rose 0.3% in October. Over the past year PCE inflation climbed to 3.8% from 3.6% in September, and core PCE, which leaves out food and energy, rose to 3.3% from 3.1%. Consumer spending, which makes up more than two-thirds of the US economy, rose 0.3%, and September's gain was revised up to 0.6%. Reuters says strong spending by higher-income households and heavy business investment in AI are helping keep inflation well above the Fed's 2% target. The data was the last major inflation report before the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, where the policy rate currently sits at 3.75%-4.00%.
rows.fact: October PCE prices rose 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier; core PCE rose 0.3% on the month and 3.3% on the year. Consumer spending increased 0.3% after a revised 0.6% gain in September. The Fed's policy rate range is 3.75%-4.00%, against a 2% inflation goal.
rows.outlook: Markets, per CME FedWatch, are pricing a quarter-point Fed hike in December and another in January, and economists expect consumer spending to slow into 2027 as inflation eats into wage gains.
rows.why: 연준이 가장 중시하는 물가 지표가 무엇이고, 목표치(2%)를 크게 웃도는 물가가 왜 추가 금리 인상 전망으로 이어지는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It explains the Fed's favorite inflation gauge and why inflation far above the 2% goal leads markets to expect more rate hikes.
rows.term_def: Inflation measured without food and energy, whose prices jump around a lot. Economists use it to see the underlying trend of price increases.
rows.note: Today's policy item (official BEA data release, Nov 25 ET). PCE and spending figures checked against BEA's October personal income and outlays release. Reuters' remark that households were saving less was left out because BEA shows the saving rate rising to 4.1%. Q3 GDP second estimate not used because it could not be confirmed on bea.gov.

opinion.title: US Core PCE Inflation Rises to 3.3% as Real Consumer Spending Stalls
opinion.author: ActionForex (staff)
opinion.summary: This market note points out that core PCE inflation rose to 3.3% year over year, slightly above the 3.2% forecast, while headline PCE reached 3.8%. Nominal spending rose 0.3%, less than the 0.4% expected, and after removing price increases real spending was flat, with services making up most of the $63.8 billion rise. Personal income jumped 0.7%, helped by one-time Medicare rebate payments, and the saving rate rose to 4.1%. The writer argues that flat real spending means households paid more rather than bought more, so the report sends a mixed signal: sticky inflation for the Fed alongside softening consumer demand.
opinion.why: 명목 지출과 실질 지출의 차이를 통해 '돈을 더 썼다'는 것이 '물건을 더 샀다'는 뜻은 아닐 수 있음을 보여 주는 좋은 예입니다.
opinion.why_en: It uses the gap between nominal and real spending to show that spending more money does not always mean buying more things.

rows.title: Biz sentiment drops for the first time in 5 months
rows.summary: The Bank of Korea's November survey showed the composite business sentiment index (CBSI) for all industries fell 0.7 point to 103.5, its first decline since June. A reading above 100 still means more firms are optimistic than pessimistic. Manufacturing sentiment slipped 0.8 point to 104.8 from October's more-than-four-year high, which the BOK linked to rising inventories and global oversupply. Non-manufacturing sentiment fell 0.7 point to 102.5 because of higher energy costs and fewer leisure activities in colder weather. The broader economic sentiment index, which also reflects consumers, dipped 0.9 point to 99.9, just below its long-run average.
rows.fact: The all-industry CBSI fell 0.7 point to 103.5 in November, the first drop in five months. Manufacturing fell to 104.8 and non-manufacturing to 102.5. The economic sentiment index (ESI) fell 0.9 point to 99.9.
rows.outlook: Firms' outlook index for December edged up 0.2 point to 102 from the previous projection.
rows.why: 기업들이 체감하는 경기를 숫자로 보여 주는 지표가 어떻게 만들어지고, 재고·에너지 비용 같은 요인이 기업 심리에 어떤 영향을 주는지 알 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a survey turns business mood into a number and how inventories and energy costs affect how firms feel about the economy.
rows.term_def: A survey-based index of how businesses feel about current and future conditions. Above 100 means more firms are optimistic than pessimistic; below 100 means the opposite.
rows.note: Today's policy item (official Bank of Korea data release, Nov 25 KST). The BOK rate decision is due Nov 26 KST, after this edition.

opinion.title: BOK's other worries ease, leaving Fed in focus
opinion.author: Kim Yeon-jae
opinion.summary: This news analysis says all 10 local brokerages surveyed expect the Bank of Korea to raise its rate to 3.25% on November 26, with most seeing the cycle peak at 3.50%. It argues domestic pressures on the BOK are easing: one-year inflation expectations fell to 2.6%, the KOSPI rebounded above 5,000, and the won strengthened to about 1,342 per dollar. Exports in the first 20 days of November doubled from a year earlier to a record $77.4 billion, with chips about half of the total. That leaves the US Federal Reserve as the main factor deciding whether the last hike comes in February or April, since a Fed hike without a BOK move would widen the rate gap between the two countries.
opinion.why: 기업 심리가 꺾이는 가운데서도 한국은행이 금리를 올리려는 이유와, 미국 금리가 한국 통화정책에 어떤 영향을 주는지 함께 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It helps explain why the Bank of Korea may still raise rates as business mood softens, and how US rates influence Korea's monetary policy.

rows.title: EU goes after Russia's banks, soldiers and athletes in new sanctions package
rows.summary: The European Commission proposed its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia since February 2022, aiming for approval in December. About 60 more Russian banks would be cut off from SWIFT, the international bank messaging system, and crypto platforms used to dodge sanctions would also be targeted. EU companies would be barred from repairing Russian energy facilities such as oil refineries damaged by Ukrainian strikes, and for the first time the ban would cover electricity services. More than 70 additional 'shadow fleet' tankers that help Russia get around the $44-per-barrel oil price cap would be blacklisted, on top of more than 670 already banned. The proposal needs the agreement of all 27 member states before it takes effect.
rows.fact: The Commission's proposal would cut about 60 more Russian banks off SWIFT, ban EU firms from servicing Russian energy infrastructure including electricity, and blacklist over 70 more shadow-fleet tankers. The G7/EU oil price cap stands at $44 a barrel. All 27 EU governments must approve the package.
rows.outlook: EU officials see China as the main route for getting around sanctions, and Brussels hopes to seal the deal in December.
rows.why: 금융 제재(SWIFT 차단)와 원유 가격상한제처럼 경제 수단이 외교·안보 정책의 도구로 어떻게 쓰이는지 구체적으로 보여 주기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows concretely how economic tools such as cutting banks off SWIFT and capping oil prices are used as instruments of foreign and security policy.
rows.term_def: A legal maximum price. Here, Western companies may ship, insure or finance Russian oil only if it is sold at or below $44 a barrel, which limits Russia's oil income.
rows.note: 7-day fallback: proposal unveiled Nov 23 (Brussels), slightly outside the 24-hour window; no stronger European policy item found for the last 24h. Measures cross-checked with UPI and bne IntelliNews reports.

opinion.title: 22nd package against Russia: is Europe's sanctions machine reaching its limits?
opinion.author: Antonia Kotseva
opinion.summary: This analysis reviews the package's measures, including the SWIFT cut-off for about 60 banks, a new crypto sanctions task force, over 70 shadow-fleet ships and more than 100 military-industrial entities. Its main argument is that the proposal is not law yet, because unanimity is required and earlier packages were held up by countries such as Hungary and Slovakia. It notes that shipping-heavy Greece, Cyprus and Malta have pushed back on maritime measures, which matters because shadow-fleet rules are central to cutting Russia's oil revenue. The author concludes that each new round is harder to pass and enforce, though she gives no numeric estimate of its economic impact.
opinion.why: 제재의 효과가 내용뿐 아니라 27개국 만장일치라는 정치적 절차와 각국의 경제적 이해관계에 따라 달라진다는 점을 이해할 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that a sanction's impact depends not just on its content but on unanimity among 27 countries and each one's economic interests.

rows.title: Industrial production up 32nd straight month on strong AI demand
rows.original_source: Central News Agency (Tseng Yun-ting and Frances Huang)
rows.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs said its industrial production index rose 29.80% from a year earlier in October to 151.30, the 32nd straight month of annual growth. Manufacturing, which is more than 90% of total output, grew 31.63%. Output of computers and optoelectronics more than doubled, up 130.57%, driven by AI servers and network switches, while machinery rose 26.85% as chipmakers added capacity and electronic components rose 25.39%. Car and car-parts output fell 3.92% as some suppliers cut inventory, showing the boom is concentrated in AI-related products. For January to October, industrial production rose 21.52%.
rows.fact: October industrial production rose 29.80% year on year to 151.30, and manufacturing rose 31.63%. Computers and optoelectronics jumped 130.57%, while cars and parts fell 3.92%. Output for the first ten months was up 21.52%.
rows.outlook: MOEA expects November manufacturing output to grow about 22% to 26% year on year and the full-year 2026 manufacturing index to rise more than 20% to a record.
rows.why: AI 투자 붐이 한 나라의 산업 생산 구조를 얼마나 빠르게 바꾸는지, 그리고 특정 산업 쏠림이 어떤 위험을 낳는지 생각해 보게 합니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how fast the AI investment boom is reshaping an economy's industrial output and raises the risk of depending on one industry.
rows.term_def: A comparison of one period with the same period a year earlier. It removes seasonal patterns, such as holiday months, so you can see the real trend.
rows.note: Today's policy item (official MOEA data release, Nov 24). Index level and month-on-month gain cross-checked with BigGo Finance's report.

opinion.title: Taiwan's AI windfall rests on strong foundations
opinion.author: Min-Hua Chiang
opinion.summary: University of Maryland Global Campus economist Min-Hua Chiang notes that information and communications technology goods made up 44% of Taiwan's exports in January-September 2026, up from 14% in 2021. Taiwan faces a 10% US tariff, lower than the 12.5% on Japan and South Korea, and traditional exporters have shifted sales from China to the US and Southeast Asia. AI-driven stock trading lifted tax revenue by about 25% in January-July, and unemployment was 3.4% in August. She argues Taiwan's manufacturing skills and flexibility should carry it through if the AI boom slows, while listing risks such as weaker US AI spending, limited land and energy, and household debt above 90% of GDP.
opinion.why: AI 호황이 수출·세수·고용에 주는 효과와 함께, 한 산업에 대한 의존이 커질 때의 위험을 균형 있게 짚어 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It weighs the AI boom's benefits for exports, tax revenue and jobs against the risks of relying heavily on one industry.
